Ground Truth: nopCommerce supports multi-vendor and drop shipping, allowing products from multiple independent vendors to appear in a common product catalog. Each vendor can be assigned an admin portal to manage their own products, review sales reports, and view order details.

All customer payments go to the store administrator's merchant account. The store owner then manually distributes funds to vendors based on order history, which is tracked separately per vendor. The customer only sees one charge from the main company.
To add a new vendor, navigate to Customers → Vendors and click the 'Add new' button. The Vendors window will be displayed.

When creating a vendor, the following details must be defined in the Vendor Info panel: Name, Description, Email (used for 'Order placed' notifications), Active status checkbox, Picture upload, and an optional Admin comment for internal use.
Some vendor message templates — specifically OrderPaid.VendorNotification and OrderPlaced.VendorNotification — are disabled by default and must be manually enabled.

Assigning a vendor to a customer record is optional. It is only required if the vendor needs to log in to the administration portal to manage their products, orders, or other data. If not needed, the store owner manages all vendor mappings.
To assign a vendor to a customer, navigate to Customers → Customers and edit the customer record. In the Customer info panel, the 'Vendors' customer role must be selected in the Customer roles field.
A vendor customer account cannot belong to the default Administrators customer role. Vendor accounts and administrator accounts are mutually exclusive.

In the Customer info panel, the 'Manager of vendor' field is used to link the customer to a specific previously created vendor record. Once linked, the customer can log in to the vendor portal and manage products, orders, shipments, and reports.
Vendor settings are configured by navigating to Configuration → Settings → Vendor settings. This page supports multi-store configuration, allowing settings to be defined globally or per store.

The Common panel in Vendor settings includes a setting to 'Allow customers to apply for vendor account'. When a customer submits a request, it creates a vendor account and notifies the store owner via email. The store owner must then manually add the customer to the 'Vendors' role to grant admin access.
If the 'Allow customers to apply for vendor account' setting is enabled, an additional option appears to require vendors to accept Terms of Service during registration.

The Catalog panel in Vendor settings allows configuration of the following options: Allow customers to contact vendors via contact forms on vendor detail pages, Allow customers to search by vendor on the advanced search page, Show vendor on the product details page, Show vendor name on the order details page, and set the number of vendors to display in the vendor navigation block.

Administrators can create custom vendor attributes (e.g., business name or website) by clicking 'Add new' in the vendor attributes section. Each attribute requires a Name and a Required flag. If marked Required, vendors must provide a value for this attribute before proceeding.
The Dashboard is the first page displayed after logging in to the nopCommerce admin area. It provides a high-level overview of store statistics.

The Dashboard displays the following store statistics: total number of orders processed (by year, month, or week), number of registered customers, count of low-stock products, and the most popular products in the store.

The Dashboard includes these informational blocks: order diagrams (last week/month/year), customer registration diagrams, order totals summary (last day/week/month/year), orders by status, incomplete orders, latest orders, popular search keywords, and bestsellers by quantity and by amount.
The Order Summary report can be filtered by: Start date, End date, Order status (e.g., Complete), Payment status (e.g., Paid), Category, Manufacturer, and Billing country.

The Order Summary report supports grouping results by time period: Day (displays individual dates), Week (displays week date ranges), or Month (displays month/year labels). After selecting filters and grouping, click 'Run report' to generate results.
To view low stock reports, navigate to Reports → Low stock. A low stock report lists all products where current stock quantity falls below the defined minimum stock quantity threshold.

The Low stock report can be filtered by the Published property, which corresponds to the published/unpublished status of the product. From the displayed results, clicking 'View' redirects to the product details page where stock quantity can be updated.
To view bestseller reports, navigate to Reports → Bestsellers. The report breaks down best-selling products based on both units sold and total revenue.

The Bestsellers report supports the following search filters: Start date, End date, Store, Order status (All/Pending/Processing/Complete/Cancelled), Payment status (All/Pending/Authorized/Paid/Refunded/Partially refunded/Voided), Category, Manufacturer, Billing country, and Vendor. Click 'Run report' to generate results.
To view products that have never been purchased, navigate to Reports → Products never purchased. The report can be filtered by Category, Manufacturer, Store, Vendor, Start date, and End date.
To view a country sales report, navigate to Reports → Country sales. Filters include: Start date, End date, Order status, Payment status, and Store. Click 'Run report' to generate results.
Customer reports are accessible via Reports → Customer reports. This section provides store owners with general information about registered customers and their order activity.
Navigate to Reports → Customer reports → Registered customers to view the number of customers registered within specific periods: last day, week, two weeks, month, and year.

Navigate to Reports → Customer reports → Customers by order total to view order totals and number of orders per customer. Filters include: Registration Start/End date, Order status, Payment status, and Shipping status. Click 'Run report' to generate results.

Navigate to Reports → Customer reports → Customers by number of orders to view the top 20 customers based on total number of orders placed. Filters include: Registration Start/End date, Order status, and Payment status.
To manage topics, navigate to Content management → Topics (pages). Topics are free-form content blocks that can be displayed on your site either embedded within other pages or on a separate page.
To search for topics in the topics list, enter the topic text or its fragment in the Search keywords field, or filter by a certain store.
To add a new topic, go to Content management → Topics (pages) and click Add new. In the Info panel, enter the Title and add the topic content using the Body field editor.

The URL field is informational only and reflects the topic's public store URL. To change it, edit the Search engine friendly page name field in the SEO panel. If left blank, the URL is formed from the page name.

In the Display panel, select the Published checkbox to make the topic visible in the public store. A topic can be included in the top menu, footer column 1, footer column 2, footer column 3, and sitemap by selecting the corresponding checkboxes.
Select the Password protected checkbox to restrict access to the topic with a password. Customers must enter the password on the topic page to view the content.

Use the Customer roles dropdown to restrict which customer roles can access a topic. To use this functionality, the setting Configuration → Catalog settings → Ignore ACL rules (sitewide) must be disabled.
Use the Limited to stores dropdown to restrict which stores display the topic. To use this functionality, the setting Catalog settings → Ignore 'limit per store' rules (sitewide) must be disabled.
Use the Accessible when store closed field to make a topic accessible even when the store is closed.
In the SEO panel, enter Meta title, Meta keywords, and Meta description for the topic. The meta description tag is a brief and concise summary of the page content.

It is possible to use the same system name for different topics. For example, two topics with the same system name can be made accessible to different customer roles (e.g. Guest vs. Registered), so each group sees different content.
While editing an existing topic or after clicking 'Save and continue edit' for a new one, the Preview button can be used to see how the topic will appear in the public store.
To manage blog posts, go to Content management → Blog posts. Click Add new and fill in the information about the new blog post.
If more than one language is enabled, select the language from the Language dropdown when creating or editing a blog post. Customers will only see blog posts in their selected language.
Enter the Title and Body text of the blog post. A Body overview can be specified so only a portion of the text appears on the main blog listing page where all posts are listed.

Enter Tags as a comma-separated list of keywords associated with the blog post. These are displayed on the blog page in the public store. The more blog posts associated with a particular tag, the larger it appears in the 'Popular tags' area in the sidebar.
Enter Meta description for the blog post header. The meta description tag is a brief and concise summary of the page content.

To manage blog comments, go to Content management → Blog comments. Use the Approve selected button to approve comments and Disapprove selected to disapprove them. Comments can also be edited or deleted; if deleted, they are permanently removed from the system.
Blog settings are managed under Configuration → Settings → Blog settings. This page supports basic and advanced modes, and enables multi-store configuration so settings can differ per store.
To manage news, go to Content management → News items. News is displayed in your store on the home page or in the site footer menu.

To add a new news item, click Add new and fill in the news item information. In the Info panel, if more than one language is enabled, select the language from the Language dropdown. Customers will only see news in their selected language.

Enter the Title of the news item (e.g., 'The launch of our new nopCommerce store'). Enter a Short description in the Short description field — this is the text visitors see on the news list in the public store.
Enter a Meta description for the news item header. The meta description tag is a brief and concise summary of the page content.

To manage news comments, go to Content management → News comments. Use the Approve selected button to approve comments and Disapprove selected to disapprove them. Comments can also be edited or deleted.
News settings are managed under Configuration → Settings → News settings. This page supports basic and advanced modes and enables multi-store configuration so settings can differ per store.
To view all polls and add new ones, go to Content management → Polls. To search for polls used in a specific store, select the store name from the list.

To add a new poll, click the Add new button in the top right. If more than one language is enabled, select the language from the Language dropdown. Customers will only see polls in their selected language.
Enter the descriptive Name of the poll — this is the text customers will see (e.g., 'What do you think about our store?'). Select the Published checkbox to make the poll active.
Select the Show polls on home page checkbox to display the poll on the home page. Select the Allow guests to vote checkbox to enable non-registered users to vote in the poll.
Enter the Start date and End date in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to control when the poll is active.

Use the Limited to stores field to enable the poll for specific stores only. Leave the field empty to show the poll in all stores. To use this, the Catalog settings → Ignore 'limit per store' rules (sitewide) setting must be disabled.
In the System keyword field, specify where the poll will be displayed on the storefront. For example, entering 'LeftColumnPoll' places it in the left column widget zone.
Enter the Display order for the poll. A value of 1 represents the top of the list.

After clicking Save and continue edit, proceed to the Poll answers panel. For each answer, enter the Name that will be displayed to a customer and the Display order (a value of 1 represents the top of the list). Click the Add new record button to save each answer.

To access message templates, go to Content management → Message templates. Several message templates are available by default to notify users and the store owner about order statuses and other events.

Search for message templates by entering keywords, which are used to search in the name, body, or subject of a template. You can also filter by store (shown when more than one store exists and the 'Ignore limit per store' setting is not active) or by Is active status.

Find the message template to edit and click Edit. If more than one language is installed, select the required language tab. By default, only English is used in the system. Languages are managed in Configuration → Language.
Edit the Subject of the message template. Tokens can be included in the subject. The full list of allowed tokens is displayed at the top of the edit page.
The Email account dropdown appears when the store has two or more email accounts configured. Email accounts are set up under Configuration → Email accounts.

Select Is active to indicate the message should be sent. Select the Send immediately checkbox to send the email right away. If Send immediately is not checked, the Delay send field is displayed to configure a send delay.
Select the Attached static file checkbox to upload a file that will be attached to every email sent using this template.

Use the Limited to stores field to restrict a message template to specific stores only. Leave the field empty for all stores. To use this functionality, the Catalog settings → Ignore 'limit per store' rules (sitewide) setting must be disabled.
Use Send test email to preview a template. Enter an email address in the Send email to field, fill in tokens with test values, then click Send.
To create a full copy of a message template, click Copy template in the top right of the edit page.

Starting with version 4.90, the main menu and footer navigation can be fully customized by the administrator. To manage menus, navigate to Content management → Menus. From this page, you can edit an existing menu or create a new one.
When creating a new menu, specify its location using the Menu type field. Options are: Main menu (the primary navigation bar) or Footer (the navigation links in the site footer).
Multiple Main menu instances can be created, but only one will be displayed on the storefront at any given time, determined by its availability and creation order.

The 'Display all categories' setting automatically generates top-level menu items based on the store's categories and their sub-categories. When enabled, these category links appear before any manually created menu items.

Menu items can link to: a specific vendor's page (Vendor), a selected topic page (Topic/page), a manually specified URL (Custom link), or display non-clickable text with no link (Text without link) — useful for parent-level header items.
For menus with the Footer type, the 'Parent menu item' property is unavailable because footer navigation supports only a single level with no nesting.

For menu items that use a grid or list template (e.g., displaying all categories), the following options are available: Number of elements per row (grid) — sets the maximum items per row; Number of subcategories per category item (grid) — sets the maximum sub-category links displayed within each grid tile.
To add a new product, navigate to Catalog → Products and click the 'Add new' button in the top right corner.
The Add a New Product page is available in two modes: Advanced (default) and Basic. Basic mode shows only required fields. The fields shown in Basic mode are configurable via the Settings button.
A product must have a Name entered before it can be saved.
A product can be assigned to multiple categories simultaneously. Categories are managed at Catalog → Categories.
A product can be assigned to multiple manufacturers simultaneously. Manufacturers are managed at Catalog → Manufacturers.
The 'Published' checkbox must be selected for a product to be visible in the public store.
Product tags are entered as comma-separated keywords. The more products associated with a tag, the larger it appears in the Popular Tags cloud on the catalog sidebar.
GTIN must conform to a recognized global trade item number standard: UPC (North America), EAN (Europe), JAN (Japan), or ISBN (Books).
Required product IDs must be entered separated by commas, and there must be no circular references (e.g., Product A requires B, and B requires A is not allowed).
The Admin Comment field is for internal use only and is never visible to customers.
A product must be one of two types: Simple Product or Grouped Product (product with variants).
Simple products can optionally be marked as Rental products, which requires specifying a rental period (e.g., hours, days, weeks, months).

Selecting 'Visible individually' makes the product appear in catalog and search results. If unchecked, the product is hidden from the catalog and is only accessible from a grouped product's details page.
If Old Price is set to a value greater than zero, it becomes visible in the public store alongside the current price for comparison.
Product Cost is for internal use only and is never displayed to customers.
When 'Customer enters price' is enabled, a Minimum Amount and Maximum Amount must be defined for the price range the customer can enter.
When 'Available for pre-order' is enabled, a Pre-order availability start date field is displayed. The Pre-order button changes to Add to Cart when this date is reached.
PAngV (base price) is required by German law. For example, if selling 500mL of beer for €1.50, the base price of €3.00 per 1L must also be displayed.
A product must be either marked as 'Tax Exempt' or assigned to a Tax Category. Tax categories are managed under Configuration → Tax → Tax Categories.
If 'Shipping Enabled' is selected, the product's Weight, Length, Width, and Height must be provided for shipping cost calculation. Measures are configured at Configuration → Shipping → Measures.
If 'Ship Separately' is enabled, every unit of the product in an order is shipped in its own separate box.
A product must use one of three inventory methods: 'Don't Track Inventory', 'Track Inventory', or 'Track Inventory by Product Attributes'.
Stock Quantity is reduced automatically whenever an order is shipped.

A Minimum Cart Quantity can be set to enforce a minimum number of units a customer must purchase (e.g., minimum of 3). A Maximum Cart Quantity can be set to limit how many units a customer can purchase at once.
If 'Allowed Quantities' is specified as a comma-separated list, customers can only purchase the product in exactly those quantities, presented as a dropdown instead of a free-entry quantity field.
The 'Display Stock Quantity' checkbox is only available when the 'Display Availability' checkbox is also selected.
When using 'Track Inventory by Product Attributes', multiple warehouse management is not supported for that product.

Multiple product images can be uploaded at once. Each image requires an Alt text, Title text, and Display Order. If Alt or Title text is empty, the system uses a default rule (e.g., the product name).
To upload images in SVG format, a specific setting must first be activated in the store configuration.
Attribute value type can be 'Simple' or 'Associated to Product'. The 'Associated to Product' type links the attribute value to another catalog product and also tracks that product's stock separately.
When an attribute value is 'Associated to Product', the administrator must select the associated product and verify there are no warnings before saving.
When 'Customer enters quantity' is disabled for an 'Associated to Product' value, a fixed Product Quantity must be specified. The minimum allowed value is 1.
An Overridden Price set on an attribute combination replaces the base product price entirely. All other attribute-level price adjustments are ignored when an overridden price is specified.
A picture associated with an attribute combination replaces the main product image when the customer selects that combination.
Specification attributes are for informational display only and cannot affect pricing or purchasing behavior, unlike product attributes.
Gift card products cannot be automatically added to the cart as required products because they have mandatory built-in attributes (recipient information) that must be filled in manually.
A product marked as a Gift Card must have its type specified as either 'Physical' or 'Virtual'.
Products can be imported from Excel only. Products can be exported to XML or Excel. The export scope can be 'all found' or 'selected' products. The catalog can also be downloaded as PDF.
The Bulk Edit Products page is accessed via Catalog → Products → Bulk Edit Products. It was introduced as a native feature in nopCommerce 4.80; prior versions required a third-party plugin.
Before editing, products can be filtered by: Category, Manufacturer, Vendor, Warehouse, Product Type, and Publication Status.
The following fields are editable inline in the bulk edit grid: Product Name, SKU, Price, Old Price, Stock Quantity, and Published status.
The Manage Inventory Method field is displayed in the bulk edit grid as read-only and cannot be changed via bulk edit.
Bulk save (selected)' applies changes only to products checked in the grid. 'Bulk save (all)' applies changes to all products currently visible in the grid, regardless of selection.

Changes made in the bulk edit grid are not persisted to the database until one of the save buttons is explicitly clicked. When saved, the product's UpdatedOnUtc timestamp is automatically set to the current UTC time.

If stock quantities change (e.g., due to customer orders) while the bulk edit page is open, saving will overwrite the current database value with the stale value from when the page was loaded, potentially causing incorrect stock levels.

Only a limited subset of product fields is editable via bulk edit. Fields such as full description, images, shipping parameters, tax settings, product attributes, and SEO fields require individual product pages or Excel import/export.
In nopCommerce 4.80+, access to the Bulk Edit Products page is governed by ACL. Granular permissions allow separate control over viewing, editing, and deleting products independently.
Product attributes are defined globally at Catalog → Attributes → Product Attributes before being applied to individual products. By default, no product attributes are pre-created.

When creating a new product attribute, the Name field is required. The Description field is optional. After saving, the administrator must click 'Save and continue edit' to proceed to the Predefined Values panel.
Predefined attribute values are optional at the time of attribute creation; values can be added later when applying the attribute to a specific product.
Adding or updating Predefined Values does NOT retroactively affect products that already have that attribute applied to them.
Each predefined attribute value supports: Name, Price Adjustment (fixed or percentage), Weight Adjustment, Cost, Is Pre-selected, and Display Order.
The Cost field represents either the purchase price from third-party suppliers or the combined cost of materials and in-house manufacturing. It is not displayed to customers.

When applying an attribute to a product, the Control Type determines how it is presented to customers. Available types: Drop-down List, Radio Button List, Checkbox, Text Box, Multiline Text Box, Date Picker, File Upload, and Color Squares.

Drop-down lists, radio button lists, checkboxes, and color squares require the administrator to define specific values. Text boxes, multiline text boxes, date pickers, and file upload controls do not require predefined values.

For the Text Box control type, validation rules can be specified: Minimum Length, Maximum Length, and Default Value. For File Upload, Allowed File Extensions and Maximum File Size (KB) can be specified.
For the Date Picker control type, the number of years displayed is configured via the 'catalogsettings.countdisplayedyearsdatepicker' parameter. Setting it to zero displays only the current year.
If 'Is Required' is set for an attribute, customers must select a value for it before they can add the product to the cart.
An attribute can have a condition that makes it visible only when a specific value of a previously defined attribute has been selected by the customer.

Conditions show or hide an entire attribute — they do not filter individual values within an attribute. Cascading dropdowns are not supported out of the box. Only one condition (a single attribute + value pair) can be set per attribute.

Each attribute combination can have its own: SKU, Manufacturer Part Number, GTIN, Stock Quantity, Overridden Price, Notify Admin for Quantity Below threshold, Allow Out of Stock flag, and associated Picture.
The combination's SKU is shown in the shopping cart when that combination is selected (if 'Show SKU' is enabled in Catalog Settings). It does not appear on the product details page itself.
Control types that accept free-form customer input (File Upload, Text Box, Date Picker) are incompatible with attribute combinations and should not be used when combinations are required.

Allow only existing attribute combinations' is only visible when the inventory method is 'Track inventory by product attributes'. It restricts customers from adding combinations that don't exist or have zero stock. Invalid combinations remain visible on the product page but produce an 'Out of Stock' message when added to cart.

Tier pricing is not supported at the attribute combination level out of the box. Overridden prices on combinations can be used as a workaround, but they apply a flat price rather than quantity-based tiers.

Specification attributes are informational only — they are visible on the product details page and can be used for filtering on category pages, but they do not define product price and cannot be used for inventory tracking.

Specification attributes are defined globally at Catalog → Attributes → Specification Attributes. By default, no specification attributes are pre-created. They must be added to each product individually after creation.
A specification attribute requires a Name and a Display Order. After saving, 'Save and continue edit' is needed to access the Options panel where attribute options are defined.

Each specification attribute option requires a Name, a Display Order, and optionally an RGB color. If 'Specify color' is selected, the color swatch is shown to customers instead of the text option name.
Specification attributes can be organized into named groups with a Display Order. Attributes not assigned to any group fall into a default 'non-grouped' state.
When adding a specification attribute to a product, the following fields are configured: Attribute Type, Attribute, Attribute Option, Allow Filtering, Show on Product Page, and Display Order.
The 'Show on product page' field must be selected for the specification attribute table to be visible on the product details page in the public store.

The 'Allow filtering' field must be selected on a per-product basis to enable customers to filter by that specification attribute on category pages. The 'Enable specification attribute filtering' setting in Catalog Settings must also be active globally.
The 'Compare products' feature uses specification attributes to display side-by-side product comparisons. It must be enabled at Configuration → Settings → Catalog Settings → Compare products panel.
The 'Used by products' panel on a specification attribute shows all products that currently have that attribute applied.
To make a product downloadable, the 'Is download' checkbox must be selected on the product edit page. The download file can be uploaded directly or provided as an external download URL.
Since downloadable products require no physical shipping, the 'Shipping enabled' checkbox must be left unchecked in the Shipping panel.
Downloads can be set to unlimited, or restricted by a Maximum Number of Downloads and/or a Number of Days during which the customer retains access.
Download activation type must be one of two options: 'When Order Is Paid' (automatic upon payment) or 'Manually' (administrator must activate the download manually from the order details page).
If 'Has user agreement' is enabled, the customer must accept the agreement text before they are permitted to download the product.

A sample download file can be provided (via upload or URL). Sample files are freely downloadable by any customer without purchase, and are shown as a 'Download sample' button on the product details page.
After purchase, customers access their downloadable products from the 'My account' section. The download link becomes visible once the download is activated (automatically or manually).
The 'Downloadable products' tab on the 'My account' page can be hidden from customers using the 'Hide Downloadable products tab' setting in Configuration → Settings → Customer Settings.

To create a grouped product: first create the simple products (variants), then create a parent product with type set to 'Grouped (product with variants)', and assign the simple products in the Associated Products panel.
A simple product can only be associated with one grouped product at a time.
Grouped products are not orderable directly. Customers must order one of the associated simple products. Each associated product has its own Add to Cart button on the grouped product details page.
For each associated simple product, the 'Visible individually' checkbox controls whether it also appears independently in catalog and search results, or only on the grouped product's page.

Any product can be made recurring by enabling the recurring option and configuring: Cycle Length (numeric interval), Cycle Period (Days, Weeks, Months, or Years), and Total Cycles (number of recurrences).
For recurring products, the system automatically creates subsequent orders using the payment details of the initial order. The original shipping charges also apply to subsequent orders.

Automatic recurring order processing requires the active payment method to support automatic recurring payments (e.g., PayPal Direct). Without this support, recurring orders must be processed manually.
A rental product is created by starting with a standard Simple product and checking the 'Is rental' checkbox in the Rental panel.
A rental product requires a Rental Period Length (the minimum billing period) and a Rental Period unit (Days, Weeks, Months, or Years). The product price is specified for this period.
When purchasing a rental product, customers must specify the rental start date and end date in the public store. The total rental price updates accordingly based on the period selected.
Checkout attributes can be used to allow customers to specify a return time (e.g., for a carrier pickup), complementing the rental end date.
Products can be exported to XML (all found or selected) or Excel (all found or selected) from Catalog → Products. The catalog can also be downloaded as PDF.

The exported file contains all product characteristics from the product editing page panels (Product info, SEO, Pictures, etc.). When product attributes are used, the exported Excel table is grouped by rows.
Import is supported from Excel format only. Before importing, the official template must be downloaded from the export function to ensure correct column naming.

Column names in the import file must exactly match the template column names. Column names are case-sensitive. Not all fields are mandatory — a product will be created from whichever fields are populated.
Products during import are matched by SKU. If the SKU already exists in the store, the corresponding product is updated. If it does not exist, a new product is created.

A product deleted in nopCommerce is only marked as deleted in the database, not physically removed. Importing a file with the same SKU as a deleted product will not restore it — the import will succeed but no product will appear.
Import is memory-intensive. It is not recommended to import more than 500–1000 records at once. Larger datasets should be split into multiple files.

The Categories and Manufacturers columns can reference objects by their ID or by name. When using names, the full category hierarchy is specified using '>>' as a separator (e.g., 'Computers >> Desktops'). Category and manufacturer name matching is case-sensitive.

Importing products with images hosted on external URLs is disabled by default for security. It can be enabled via the 'Export/import products. Allow download images' setting in Catalog Settings. URLs must contain only Latin characters; special characters (e.g., ^ or ~) should be avoided.
The 'Export/import products. Allow splitting file' setting enables automatic splitting of large import files into optimal-size chunks to reduce import delays.

Product attributes and specification attributes are only included in import/export when the corresponding settings ('Export/import products with attributes' and 'Export/import products with specification attributes') are enabled in Catalog Settings.
When two or more store languages are configured, Excel/XML import and export supports multilingual product data.

Product tags are managed at Catalog → Product Tags. The list shows each tag's name and the number of products associated with it. Tags can be edited or deleted (individually or in bulk) from this page.
Tags are added to a product on the product edit page by entering keywords separated by commas. Once a tag is created, it can be reused across other products.

The more products associated with a tag, the larger that tag appears in the Popular Tags cloud displayed in the catalog sidebar. The number of tags shown in the cloud is controlled by the 'Number of product tags (cloud)' setting in Catalog Settings.

Customers can browse all products associated with a tag via the 'Products by tag' page. The page size for this page can be configured by the store owner, and optionally customers can be allowed to change it.

By default, product reviews must be approved by the store owner before they appear in the public store. This requirement can be removed by clearing the 'Product reviews must be approved' option in Configuration → Settings → Catalog Settings.
Reviews can be approved or disapproved in bulk by selecting them and clicking 'Approve selected' or 'Disapprove selected' from Catalog → Product Reviews.
The 'One review per product from customer' setting restricts each customer to a single review per product.
The 'Product review possible only after product purchasing' setting restricts the ability to leave a review to customers who have actually ordered that product.
Anonymous users can be allowed or blocked from writing reviews via the 'Allow anonymous users to write product reviews' setting in Catalog Settings.
After a review is approved and published, other customers can vote on whether it was helpful by clicking Yes or No. This helpfulness voting is visible in the public store.

Custom review types can be created to allow customers to rate multiple specific aspects of a product (e.g., quality, value, shipping). If a review type is marked as 'Required', the customer must provide a rating for it before submitting.
Rating values in the review types panel cannot be edited by the administrator — no columns in the review types table are editable.

The store owner can be notified of new product reviews via the 'Notify about new product reviews' setting. Customers can be notified of replies to their reviews via 'Notify customer about product review reply'.
The 'Reviews per store' setting controls whether customers see only reviews written in the current store or reviews from all stores on a product's details page.

Customer reviews can be enabled or disabled on a per-product basis using the 'Allow customer reviews' checkbox on the product edit page. There is no global on/off toggle for reviews across all products.
To view and manage orders, navigate to Sales → Orders. The orders page lists all current orders, and a new order appears after a customer completes a transaction.

Orders can be searched and filtered by Start date, End date, Warehouse, Order status (All, Pending, Processing, Complete, Cancelled), Payment status, Store, Vendor, Billing phone number, Billing email address, Billing last name, Billing country, Payment method, and Order notes.
To go directly to a specific order, enter the order number in the 'Go directly to order #' field and click Go.
Orders can be exported to XML or Excel (all found or selected) by clicking the Export button at the top of the orders page.

Orders can be imported from Excel using the Import button. Imported orders are distinguished by order GUID; if a GUID already exists, its details will be updated. It is not recommended to import more than 500–1,000 records at once due to memory resource requirements.

To view full order information, click View beside the order in the list. From the order details page, a store owner can generate a PDF invoice, delete the order, or view order info including Order #, creation date/time, and the customer who placed the order.
To define order settings, navigate to Configuration → Settings → Order settings. Settings support multi-store configuration, meaning different values can be set per store.
The 'Checkout disabled' setting disables the entire checkout process. 'Anonymous checkout allowed' permits customers to purchase without registering or logging in.
Use one page checkout' consolidates the checkout process into a single webpage. 'Order totals on payment info tab' displays a product list and totals in the payment info tab during one-page checkout.
Store owners can require customers to accept the Terms of Service before processing an order — either on the shopping cart page or on the confirm order page.

The 'Disable Billing address step during checkout' setting pre-fills billing address from default registration data. This cannot be used with guest checkout. Ensure address fields that cannot be pre-filled are not required in Configuration → Settings → Customer settings.
Disable Order completed page' automatically redirects customers to the order details page after an order is placed, instead of showing the order completed page.
A minimum order sub-total amount can be set; orders below this amount will not be issued. Tax can optionally be included when validating this minimum.

A minimum order total amount can be set; orders below this amount will not be issued. 'Auto update order totals' (currently BETA) automatically recalculates order totals when editing an order in the admin area.
The Order ID counter can be set to a custom starting number; this only affects orders created after the change and must be greater than the current maximum order ID.

A custom order number mask can be defined (e.g., using {YYYY} to prefix orders with the creation year). 'Is re-order allowed' enables customers to re-order, automatically adding all items from a previous order to the cart.
Complete order when delivered' sets order status to Complete only when shipping status is Delivered.
Shipments are managed from within the order details page, accessible via Sales → Orders. Each shipment can have a tracking number set, an admin comment added, and the total shipment weight viewed.
From the shipment details page, a store owner can mark the shipment as Shipped, edit the Date shipped, mark it as Delivered, edit the Date delivered, print a packaging slip, or delete the shipment.
If a customer selected 'Pick up in store' during checkout, the shipment can be marked as 'Ready for pickup' instead of shipped.
To view and edit return requests, navigate to Sales → Return requests. All submitted return requests are displayed in a list, and clicking Edit opens the return request details window.
Return requests are only available for completed orders. A customer cannot submit a return request for orders that are not in a completed status.

Return request settings are configured in Configuration → Settings → Order settings under the Return request settings panel. The 'Enable returns system' checkbox must be selected to allow customers to submit return requests.

A custom return request number mask can be defined. A 'Number of days that the return request is available' field controls how long after purchase the return link is visible to customers (e.g., 30 days).

To submit a return request, a customer goes to My Account → Orders, clicks 'Return Item(s)' beside a completed order, and then selects the quantity to return, the return reason, and the desired return action.
Customers can optionally attach files to a return request when the 'Allow file uploads' setting is enabled. They can also add an optional comment in the Comments field.
After submitting a return request, customers can view their requests and statuses under My Account → Return requests in the public store.

In the return request edit view, the store owner can view the return request ID, associated Order #, and the customer's email — clicking the order number or customer email redirects to the respective detail pages.

Store owners can define custom return reasons and return actions via the Return request settings panel. New actions are added by clicking 'Add new' and providing a name and display order (1 represents the first item in the list).

To view all shopping carts and wishlists across all customers and stores, navigate to Sales → Shopping carts and wishlists. Select the desired type (Shopping cart or Wishlist) in the Search area and click Search.

The shopping cart list shows all products added to carts but not yet purchased (abandoned carts). From this list, you can navigate to the customer details page or the product edit page, or delete a product from the cart.

Shopping cart settings are configured at Configuration → Settings → Shopping cart settings. Options include: Show discount box, Show gift card box, Show mini-shopping cart, Maximum shopping cart items, and Carts shared between stores.
Display cart after adding a product' shows the shopping cart page immediately after a product is added. If disabled, the customer remains on the product page after adding to cart.
The number of cross-sell products displayed on the shopping cart checkout page can be configured. Enter 0 to disable cross-sells.

The mini shopping cart dropdown, which appears at the top right corner when hovering over the Shopping cart link, can be enabled. When enabled, the maximum number of products shown in the mini cart can also be configured.

A wishlist is a list of products a customer can save to transfer to the cart later or share with friends. A product's 'Add to wishlist' button appears on the product details page if adding to wishlist is enabled for that product.

When a product with variants is added to a wishlist, all selected variants are included. If the same product is added multiple times, it appears only once but with an updated quantity reflecting the number of times it was added.

Wishlist settings include: allow customers to email their wishlist, allow guests to email their wishlist, allow out-of-stock items to be added to the wishlist, show product images on wishlist, and display wishlist after adding a product.

Checkout attributes are used to gather additional order information during the final stage of the shopping process (on the shopping cart page). An example is a Gift wrapping option displayed in the shopping cart.
Each checkout attribute includes a Text prompt (a question or comment shown on the cart page) and a Control type such as Dropdown list, Radio button list, Checkboxes, or Textbox.

Control types that require predefined values (Dropdown list, Radio button list, Checkboxes, Color squares) must have values defined by the store owner. Textbox and Date picker controls do not require predefined values — customers fill them in.

Validation rules can be specified for certain control types. For Textbox, this includes Minimum length, Maximum length, and Default value. For File upload, Allowed file extensions and Maximum file size (KB) can be defined.

Selecting the 'Required' checkbox for a checkout attribute forces customers to provide a value before completing the purchase. After saving, the new attribute is displayed on the shopping cart page in the public store.
To set up inventory for a product, navigate to Catalog → Products, edit a product, and go to the Inventory panel within the product edit window.

There are three inventory tracking methods available: 'Don't track inventory' (for services or custom goods that do not require stock tracking), 'Track inventory' (by product), and 'Track inventory by product attributes'.

Stock quantity represents the total available quantity and is automatically reduced whenever an order is shipped. The warehouse to use for shipping rate calculation can be assigned and managed at Configuration → Shipping → Warehouses.

Selecting 'Multiple warehouses' enables inventory management and shipping from multiple locations. Per warehouse, you can define stock quantity, reserved quantity (ordered but not yet shipped/added to shipment), and planned quantity (added to shipment but not yet shipped).

Enabling 'Display availability' shows stock availability to customers in the public store. Enabling 'Display stock quantity' shows the actual quantity on the product details page (only available when Display availability is also selected).

A minimum stock quantity threshold can be set. When stock falls below this level, the configured 'Low stock activity' is triggered: Nothing (no action), Disable buy button (customers can see but not buy), or Unpublish (product is removed from the store).

A 'Notify for qty below' field triggers a notification email to the administrator when stock quantity falls below the specified value. Low stock products can also be monitored via Reports → Low stock.

Backorder mode options are: 'No backorders' (customers cannot purchase when out of stock), 'Allow qty below 0' (customers can purchase even when out of stock), and 'Allow qty below 0 and notify customer' (customers can purchase and receive an out-of-stock notification; Display availability must also be enabled).

Allow back in stock subscriptions' enables customers to subscribe to notifications when a product becomes available again. A 'Product availability range' can also be shown to customers when a product is currently unavailable.

Minimum cart qty' sets the minimum number of this product a customer must add to the cart (e.g., 3 means customers must buy at least 3). 'Maximum cart qty' sets the upper limit (e.g., 5 means customers can purchase no more than 5).
The 'Allowed quantities' field accepts a comma-separated list of specific quantities. Instead of a free-text quantity box, customers will see a dropdown with only those values.
Checking the 'Not returnable' checkbox on a product prevents customers from submitting a return request for that product.

When using 'Track inventory by product attributes', out-of-stock behavior can be configured per attribute combination. 'Allow only existing attribute combinations' restricts add-to-cart to combinations that have stock quantities greater than 0.

Gift cards are created by defining a product as a gift card via the 'Is gift card' checkbox in Catalog → Products → Add new → Gift card panel. The Gift card type (Virtual or Physical) must be specified. It is not recommended to change the gift card type in a live store.
To view and manage purchased gift cards, navigate to Sales → Gift cards. Click Edit beside a gift card to open its details.
Gift cards are disabled by default. The 'Is gift card activated' checkbox must be selected and a coupon code generated to activate a gift card manually.

To activate gift cards automatically after an order is completed, go to Configuration → Settings → Order settings → Gift cards panel and select 'Activate gift cards after completing of an order'. The coupon code will also be generated automatically.

Gift cards can also be configured to deactivate automatically when an order is cancelled ('Deactivate gift cards after cancelling of an order') or deleted ('Deactivate gift cards after deleting of an order'), and usage history can be cleared on cancellation.

Editable gift card fields include: Gift card type, Initial value, Recipient's name, Recipient's email (Virtual only), Sender's name, Sender's email (Virtual only), and an optional message. The Remaining amount field shows how much value is left.
Clicking 'Notify recipient' sends an email with gift card details to the recipient. This button is only available for Virtual gift cards, not Physical ones.

Once a gift card is activated, the customer uses it during checkout by entering the coupon code in the gift card box on the shopping cart page. The Usage history panel on the gift card details page shows all orders in which the coupon was applied.
The gift card box on the shopping cart page can be hidden by clearing the 'Show gift card box' checkbox in Configuration → Settings → Shopping cart settings (Common panel).

Customers can be allowed to check their gift card balance by enabling 'Allow customers to check gift card balance' in Configuration → Settings → Shopping cart settings. This feature requires CAPTCHA to be enabled (Configuration → Settings → General settings → CAPTCHA panel) due to security risks.
Categories must be created before products can be assigned to them.
A category must have a Name entered before it can be saved.
The Add a New Category page is available in two modes: advanced and basic. Basic mode displays only the main fields; advanced mode displays all available fields.
A category can be designated as a subcategory by selecting a Parent Category. The subcategory will be nested under the parent in the public store.
A category must have the 'Published' checkbox selected to be visible in the public store.
A category can optionally be displayed on the home page by selecting the 'Show on home page' checkbox.
A category can be included in the top navigation menu by selecting the 'Include in top menu' checkbox.
If 'Allow customers to select page size' is enabled, the store owner must provide a comma-separated list of page size options. The first value in the list is the default page size.
If 'Allow customers to select page size' is disabled, a single fixed 'Page size' value must be set instead.
Price range filtering can be enabled at the category level, with an option to allow customers to enter the price range manually by specifying 'Price from' and 'Price to' values.
Display order uses ascending numeric order. The category with display order 1 appears at the top of the list in the public store.

Discounts mapped to a category are applied to all products within that category. Only discounts of the 'Assigned to categories' type are eligible. The 'Ignore discounts (sitewide)' setting in Catalog Settings → Performance must be disabled for discounts to apply.

Access to a category can be restricted to specific customer roles via the 'Limited to customer roles' field. This requires the 'Ignore ACL rules (sitewide)' setting to be disabled in Catalog Settings.
A category can be restricted to specific stores via the 'Limited to stores' field. This requires the 'Ignore limit per store rules (sitewide)' setting to be disabled in Catalog Settings.
If the 'Restrict from vendors' option is enabled, vendors cannot assign products to that category from the Add/Edit product pages in the admin area.
A category must be saved before products can be added to it via the Products panel.
Products assigned to a category can be individually configured as 'Is featured product' and given a display order within that category.
If the SEO 'Search engine friendly page name' field is left blank, the category URL is automatically formed from the category name. If a custom value is entered, that value is used as the URL slug.

Categories can be exported to XML or Excel for backup purposes, and imported from Excel. Import column names must exactly match the downloaded template. Importing more than 500–1000 records at once is not recommended due to memory constraints.
A manufacturer must have a Name entered before it can be saved.
The Add a New Manufacturer page is available in two modes: advanced and basic. Basic mode displays only the main fields; advanced mode displays all available fields.
A manufacturer must have the 'Published' checkbox selected to be visible in the public store.
If 'Allow customers to select page size' is enabled, the store owner must provide a comma-separated list of page size options. The first value in the list is the default page size.
If 'Allow customers to select page size' is disabled, a single fixed 'Page size' value applies to the manufacturer's product listing page.

Access to a manufacturer can be restricted to specific customer roles via the 'Limited to customer roles' field. This requires the 'Ignore ACL rules (sitewide)' setting to be disabled in Catalog Settings.
A manufacturer can be restricted to specific stores via the 'Limited to stores' field. This requires the 'Ignore limit per store rules (sitewide)' setting to be disabled in Catalog Settings.
A manufacturer must be saved before products can be added to it via the Products panel.
Products assigned to a manufacturer can be individually configured as 'Is featured product' and given a display order within that manufacturer's listing.
If the SEO 'Search engine friendly page name' field is left blank, the manufacturer URL is automatically formed from the manufacturer name.

Manufacturers can be exported to XML or Excel for backup purposes, and imported from Excel. Import column names must exactly match the downloaded template. Importing more than 500–1000 records at once is not recommended due to memory constraints.
Catalog Settings supports multi-store configuration, meaning settings can be defined globally or overridden per store.
If 'Search enabled' is disabled, the search functionality is hidden from the public store entirely.
If 'Search autocomplete enabled' is active, the number of autocomplete results, whether product images are shown, and whether a link to all results is shown can each be configured independently.
A minimum search term length can be configured; customers cannot search with fewer characters than this threshold.
If 'Allow customers to search with manufacturer name' is enabled, manufacturer names are included as searchable fields. The same applies independently for category names.
Product reviews must be approved by a store administrator before being published if the 'Product reviews must be approved' setting is enabled.
If 'Product review possible only after product purchasing' is enabled, only customers who have previously ordered the product can submit a review.
If 'Reviews per store' is enabled, only reviews submitted for the current store are displayed on the product details page.
Enabling 'Ignore ACL rules (sitewide)' in the Performance panel disables all customer role access restrictions set on categories, manufacturers, and products across the entire store.
Enabling 'Ignore limit per store (sitewide)' in the Performance panel disables all store-specific restrictions on entities. It is recommended when running only a single store.
Cache product prices' must not be enabled when using complex discounts, discount requirement rules, or coupon codes, as it can result in incorrect pricing.

If 'Allow product sorting' is enabled, individual sort options (Position, Name, Price, Date of creation) can be independently activated or deactivated. Selecting 'Position' places no restriction on sort order.
If 'Include products from subcategories' is enabled, products from child categories are included when browsing a parent category page.

If 'Enable specification attribute filtering' is disabled in Catalog pages settings, specification attribute filters will not appear on catalog pages even if specification attributes exist on products.

If 'Display From prices' is enabled, the minimum possible product price based on attribute adjustments is shown instead of the base price. Enabling 'Cache product prices' is also recommended in this case, with the caveat around complex discounts.
The Product URL structure type determines the format of product page URLs; possible values are /Product, /Category/Product, and /Manufacturer/Product.

If 'Allow viewing of unpublished product details page' is enabled, unpublished products remain indexable by search crawlers, though they are not visible to customers. Store owners always retain access to unpublished products.
Product attributes and specification attributes are only included in import/export operations if the corresponding export/import settings are enabled in Catalog Settings.
When two or more store languages are configured, Export/Import to Excel and XML supports multilingual product data.

The AI content generation feature supports three providers (DeepSeek, Gemini, ChatGPT), but only one provider can be active at a time. It can be enabled or disabled independently for product descriptions and SEO meta fields.
AI-generated SEO meta tags will only populate fields that are currently empty; the tool will not overwrite existing manually entered data.
If unsaved changes exist on a product edit page, the system will prompt the user to save before sending a request to the AI service for SEO generation.
Full-text Search is not built into nopCommerce core; it requires installation of a paid plugin — either the Lucene plugin or the Elasticsearch plugin.
Unlike the standard search (which relies on exact matches), Full-text Search analyzes the entire site content to return the most relevant results, with support for fuzzy matching and typo tolerance.

Both the Lucene and Elasticsearch plugins support three search modes: Fuzzy (tolerates misspellings using edit-distance matching), Wildcard/Contains (matches partial terms using the * operator), and Exact (strict token match).

If 'Immediately update indexes' is enabled, product index changes (e.g., name or description updates) are applied in real time. If disabled, reindexing is scheduled. A manual 'Rebuild index' action is always available.
A Result limit can be configured to cap the maximum number of matches returned from the search index per query.
Additional delimiter characters can be configured to split search queries into terms. Search queries are always split by spaces in addition to any configured delimiters.
The Elasticsearch plugin requires a separately installed and configured Elasticsearch server (v8.x). The node endpoint URL and index name must be configured in the plugin settings.
The Elasticsearch plugin supports multiple authentication methods for accessing the cluster: Basic authentication (username and password) or API Key (bearer token).
The Elasticsearch plugin automatically matches the available indexing language to the current store language.
Both Full-text Search plugins belong to the 'Search provider' plugin group and can be enabled or disabled via the Enable/Disable buttons on the plugin configuration page.
To view and manage discounts, navigate to Promotions → Discounts. The page allows searching by Start date, End date, and other criteria.
Discounts can be applied to categories, products, order total, order subtotal, shipping, and manufacturers. Products can have any number of discounts attached simultaneously.

By default, no discounts exist in nopCommerce. When multiple discounts apply, the system automatically calculates the best possible price for the customer based on all available discounts and group memberships.

The most common discount method is a coupon code, which customers enter on the shopping cart page before checkout. It is recommended to use coupon codes rather than codeless discounts, as they allow tracking of campaign results.
To add a new discount, go to Promotions → Discounts and click 'Add new'. The form is available in Basic mode (main fields only) or Advanced mode (all available fields).

When creating a discount, the 'Is active' checkbox must be selected to activate it. A Name and Discount type must be provided. Discount types include: Assigned to order total, Assigned to products, Assigned to categories, Assigned to manufacturers, Assigned to shipping, and Assigned to order subtotal.

Discounts can be time-based using Start date and End date fields. The 'Cumulative with other discounts' option allows customers to apply multiple discounts simultaneously. A Discount limitation can be set, such as limiting use to once per customer.

Discount requirements can be configured to restrict who qualifies. The built-in requirement type is 'Must be assigned to a customer role'. Additional requirement types are available as marketplace plugins.

Requirement groups can be created for complex multi-rule discounts using Boolean AND/OR logic. Groups can be nested and reused as templates. Groups can be included within other groups for advanced scenarios.

For 'Assigned to products' discount type, products are added in the 'Applied to products' panel after saving the discount. A Maximum discounted quantity field controls how many items the discount applies to per order.
For discounts to function, the 'Ignore discounts (sitewide)' setting must be disabled under Configuration → Settings → Catalog settings → Performance panel.
To manage the reward points program, go to Configuration → Settings → Reward points. This page supports multi-store configuration, allowing settings to differ per store.

The Reward Points feature is a loyalty program allowing customers to earn points for specific actions such as registering and making purchases. Reward points can be redeemed as a payment method during checkout alongside other methods such as credit cards and gift cards.
Reward points are only applicable to registered users. Points can also be canceled if a customer cancels an order or submits a return request.
To activate reward points, the 'Enabled' checkbox must be selected. An Exchange rate must be defined (e.g., 1 point = $1). A Minimum reward points to use can be set; enter 0 to skip this restriction.

The 'Maximum reward points to use per order' field limits how many points a customer can redeem per order. The 'Maximum redeemed rate' limits the percentage of order total that can be paid with reward points (e.g., 0.6 = 60%). Setting either to 0 disables the restriction.

If 'Activate points immediately' is selected, customers can use reward points right after earning them. If deselected, a delay period (in days or hours) must be configured before points become usable.

The 'Display how much will be earned' option shows customers their projected points on the checkout page. The 'Points accumulated for all stores' option merges reward point balances across all stores so points earned in one store can be used in another.

Reward points can be manually added or deducted per customer via the customer management page. Entering a negative value reduces the customer's points. A validity period (in days) can be set for any points awarded.
To manage affiliates, navigate to Promotions → Affiliates. Click 'Add new' to register a new affiliate partner.

Affiliates are third-party partners who refer customers to the store. nopCommerce tracks these referrals so the store owner can determine commissions to pay. Once a customer is assigned an affiliate ID, all orders they place are tagged with that affiliate ID.

An affiliate partner link takes the format: http://www.yourstore.com/?AffiliateID=N (where N is the affiliate's ID). Store owners can also define a friendly URL name for marketing use, e.g., http://www.yourstore.com/?affiliate=friendly_name_here.
When a visitor clicks an affiliate link, nopCommerce reads the AffiliateID query string parameter from the URL to track the referral. This tracking is automatic once the link is clicked.

When adding a new affiliate, the 'Active' checkbox must be selected to activate the affiliate. The affiliate details page shows all orders placed by affiliated customers in the Affiliate orders panel.

Cross-sells and related products are configured on individual product edit pages. Navigate to Catalog → Products, select a product, click Edit, and find the 'Cross-sells' and 'Related products' panels. The product must be saved before cross-sells or related products can be added.
Cross-sells and related products are marketing tools used to offer customers additional products based on their shopping behavior. Both tools can be used simultaneously on a single product.

Cross-sell products are displayed at the bottom of the checkout page. They are typically complementary items often purchased alongside the cart product, but any product from the catalog can be added. An unlimited number of cross-sell products can be linked to a product.
To add a cross-sell product, click 'Add new cross-sell product' and search the catalog using criteria such as Product name, Category, Vendor, Store, Product type, or Manufacturer.

The number of cross-sell products shown on the checkout page is controlled by the 'Number of cross-sells' setting under Configuration → Settings → Shopping cart settings. Enter 0 to disable cross-sell display entirely.

Related products are displayed below the selected product on its product details page, providing an opportunity to advertise and up-sell. An unlimited number of related products can be added to a product.
To add a related product, click 'Add new related product' and select products from the catalog using the same search criteria available for cross-sells.
To manage email campaigns, navigate to Promotions → Campaigns. Click 'Add new' to create a new campaign. To manage newsletter subscribers, navigate to Promotions → Newsletter Subscribers.

Email campaigns are sent to customers who have subscribed to newsletters. Campaigns are used to promote trust, loyalty, and sales. Examples include welcome emails, announcements, company news, and coupon distributions.
A 'Send mass email' action sends the campaign to all customers subscribed to newsletters. A test email option is also available to preview the campaign before sending it to the full subscriber list.

Newsletter subscribers can be imported from an external CSV file or exported to CSV via Promotions → Newsletter Subscribers. The required CSV format is: email_address, is_active, store_id (store_id is optional). Example: test@test.com, true.
Subscribers can be searched on the Newsletter Subscribers page by email address, active status, start date, and end date of subscription.
Customers can subscribe to newsletters during store registration or via the newsletter subscription form in the store footer (available in the Default Clean nopCommerce theme).
To manage customers, navigate to Customers → Customers. The customer list contains details of all existing customers and allows adding new ones.
In nopCommerce, customers include all users such as administrators, vendors, and buyers — not just shoppers.
Customers can be searched using one or more criteria: email, username (if enabled), first name, last name, date of birth, company, phone, zip code, IP address, active status, and customer roles.
Customer data can be exported to XML or Excel using 'Export to XML (all)', 'Export to Excel (all)', 'Export to XML (selected)', or 'Export to Excel (selected)' buttons.

To add a new customer, click the 'Add new' button in the Customers window. The Customer info panel allows entering personal and account information, changing passwords, and assigning or removing customer roles.

When creating or editing a customer, the following fields are available: email address, first name, last name, date of birth, company name, tax exempt status, newsletter subscription, customer roles, manager of vendor, active status, and admin comment.
Any customer role that requires system login (e.g., Administrator, Vendor) must also include the 'Registered' customer role. A customer can be assigned one or multiple roles.

A vendor can be associated with a customer account via the 'Manager of vendor' dropdown. Once linked, the customer can log into the vendor portal and manage its products and orders. The customer must also exist in the Vendors list.
The 'Customer must change password' checkbox can be selected to require the customer to change their password on next login.

After saving a customer record, a store owner can send an email or a private message to the customer using the 'Send email' and 'Send private message' buttons. Private messaging requires forum private messages to be enabled in forum settings.
The Orders panel on the customer details page displays the customer's order history and details.
The Addresses panel allows viewing, editing, and creating new addresses for a customer. Click 'Add new address', fill in the fields, and click Save to add the address.
The 'Current shopping cart and wishlist' panel allows a store owner to view the customer's current shopping cart and wishlist items.
The Activity log panel on the customer details page allows viewing the individual customer's activity log. Activity types are managed in the Activity log section.

The 'Place order (impersonate)' panel allows store owners to create orders on behalf of customers without requiring their password. This is useful for phone orders or CSR-assisted purchases. Click 'Place order', add products to the cart, proceed through checkout, then click 'Finish session' to end the impersonation session.
The 'Back in stock subscriptions' panel shows all products the customer has subscribed to for back-in-stock notifications.

The Reward points panel (visible when the reward points program is enabled) allows store owners to add reward points to a customer or view their reward point usage history. A message or comment can be added when awarding points. The 'Activate points immediately' checkbox controls whether points are available right away or after a delay specified in the Reward points activation field.
To manage customer roles, navigate to Customers → Customer roles.

Customer roles enable grouping of web store users (e.g., store admins, shoppers, vendors). Roles can be granted special rights such as discounted pricing, tax exemption, free shipping, and more via the access control list.
To add a new customer role, click 'Add new'. Provide a name and configure role settings including Active status, Free shipping, Tax exempt, password lifetime, and purchased-with-product triggers.
Selecting the 'Free shipping' checkbox on a customer role grants all customers in that role free shipping on their orders.
Selecting the 'Tax exempt' checkbox on a customer role enables customers in that role to make tax-free purchases.
The 'Override default tax display type' option, when selected, allows choosing a custom tax display type for that customer role from the Default tax display type dropdown.

The 'Enable password lifetime' checkbox forces customers in that role to change their passwords after a specified period. The Password lifetime days setting must also be configured in Customer Settings.

A customer can be automatically added to a role when they purchase a specific product. Use the 'Choose product' button to select the qualifying product. If an order is refunded or cancelled, the customer must be manually removed from the role.

The 'Is system role' flag indicates that a role is used internally by the application (e.g., Administrators, Forum Moderators, Registered, Guests). System roles cannot be deleted. The system name of the role is also displayed and cannot be modified.
To configure customer settings, navigate to Configuration → Settings → Customer settings. This page supports multi-store configuration.

Four registration modes are available: (1) Standard account creation — no approval required; (2) Email validation required — customers must confirm their email; (3) Administrator approval required — admin must approve each registration; (4) Registration disabled — no new registrations allowed.
Selecting 'Notify about new customer registration' sends the store owner an email notification whenever a new customer registers.
The 'Require registration for downloadable products' checkbox forces customers to complete registration before purchasing downloadable products.

The 'Allow customers to check gift card balance' option lets customers check their gift card balance. When enabled, CAPTCHA must also be activated (Configuration → Settings → General settings → CAPTCHA panel) for security purposes.

Selecting 'Usernames enabled' allows customers to register and log in using a username instead of an email address. It is not recommended to change this setting in a production environment. Sub-options include: allow username changes, check username availability, username validation rules, and regex-based validation.

Password security settings include: minimum and maximum password length, requirements for lowercase, uppercase, digits, and non-alphanumeric characters, unduplicated passwords count, password lifetime in days, password recovery link expiry (days), maximum login failures, and lockout duration (minutes).
The 'Force multi-factor authentication' option enforces MFA for customer roles specified in the Access Control List. At least one MFA provider must be active for this to work.
The 'Force entering email twice' checkbox requires customers to enter their email address twice during registration as a verification measure.
The 'Allow customers to select time zone' setting lets customers choose their time zone from their account page. When disabled, the store's default time zone is applied for all customers.
The 'Allow customers to remove associations' setting permits customers to remove their external authentication associations (e.g., social login links) from their account.

The 'Store last visited page' checkbox enables tracking and storing of the last page each customer visited. This data is visible on the Customers → Online customers page. Disabling this setting can improve site performance.

The Customer form fields panel controls which fields appear on the customer registration page. Each field can be enabled or set as required. If the default fields are insufficient, custom customer attributes can be added in the same manner as checkout attributes.

The Address form fields panel controls which address fields are available during checkout registration. Configurable fields include Company, Street address, Street address 2, Zip/postal code, Fax number, and more. Each field can be enabled and optionally set as required. Custom address attributes can also be added.
The 'Accept privacy policy enabled' checkbox requires customers to accept the privacy policy during registration.
The 'Newsletter enabled' checkbox offers customers the option to subscribe to a newsletter during registration.
To manage the Access Control List, navigate to Configuration → Access control list.

The Access Control List (ACL) restricts or grants users access to certain areas of the site. It is role-based, managing groups such as Global Administrators and Content Managers. Only users with administrator rights can access the ACL.
The roles used in the ACL are managed on the Customers → Customer roles page. Any changes to roles are reflected in ACL permissions.

To assign permissions, click the 'Edit' button next to a permission item and select the required customer roles. Predefined permission items include: Access Admin Area, Manage Blog, Manage Campaigns, Manage Forums, Manage News, Manage Newsletter Subscribers, Allow Navigation (Public Store), and Display Prices (Public Store).
A user must have administrator rights to access the ACL configuration area. The ACL itself appears in the administration area only.

The Catalog settings option 'Ignore ACL rules (sitewide)' disables all ACL rules configured for entities. This setting should only be used when ACL-based restrictions are not needed, as it improves performance but removes all access control on catalog entities.
To search and view activity logs, navigate to Customers → Activity log. To manage which activity types are tracked, navigate to Customers → Activity types.
By default, all activity types are enabled for tracking in nopCommerce. Store owners can disable specific types by clearing the relevant checkboxes on the Activity types page.
Most activity types track administrator actions in the admin area. Some activity types track public store shopper actions, such as adding items to cart or wishlist and placing orders.
To enable or disable an activity type, go to Customers → Activity types, select or deselect the 'Is enabled' checkbox next to the activity type, then click Save in the top right.
Activity logs can be searched using the following criteria: date range (Created from / Created to fields or dropdown calendar), activity log type, and IP address.

Individual customer activity logs can be viewed from the customer's detail page via the Activity log panel. Activity type management is accessible from the Activity log - Customer activity types section.
To view online customers, navigate to Customers → Online customers in the administration area.
The Online Customers window displays all customers who have been active within the last 20 minutes.

The Online Customers window includes the following columns: Customer info (clickable link to view/edit the customer), IP address, Location, Last activity (date and time of last login), and Last visited page.
To display the 'Last visited page' column for online customers, the 'Store last visited page' setting must be enabled on the Configuration → Settings → Customer settings page (Account panel).
Clicking on a customer's name or info link in the Online Customers window redirects to that customer's full details page, where the store owner can view and edit all customer information.
